# vachaka


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

vachaka wraps [Vāgdhenu](https://github.com/prathoshap/vagdhenu), a Sanskrit chant TTS (IndicF5 fine-tune, BigVGAN-v2 vocoder, Apache-2.0),
in a small API that runs on CUDA, Apple silicon or CPU, and checks each render with [Su-śrotā](https://huggingface.co/prathoshap/sushrota-sanskrit-asr),
a Sanskrit ASR, which also gives word timings by forced alignment.

Vāgdhenu is laukika chant: no Vedic svaras. The voice is its author’s; the reference clip sets pace and melody. Please disclose that the audio is
synthetic and credit Vāgdhenu.

## Install

``` sh
pip install vachaka          # rendering
pip install 'vachaka[check]' # Su-śrotā: transcripts, error rate, word timings
```

Weights download from the Hugging Face Hub on first use (about 1.5 GB for Vāgdhenu, 520 MB for Su-śrotā); Vāgdhenu’s and BigVGAN’s sources are
fetched at pinned commits into `~/.cache/vachaka` (`VACHAKA_CACHE`). Writing mp3 needs `ffmpeg`.

## Use

``` python
from vachaka.core import Chanter
from vachaka.check import Ear, best_of

ch, ear = Chanter(), Ear()
lines = ['वसुदेवसुतं देवं कंसचाणूरमर्दनम्', 'देवकीपरमानन्दं कृष्णं वन्दे जगद्गुरुम्']
r = best_of(partial(ch.chant, lines), ear, ' '.join(lines))
r.spans                                   # [(0, 4230), (4980, 9550)]: one span per line, ms
ear.words(r, [l.split() for l in lines])  # [[['वसुदेवसुतं', 120, 1279], ...], ...]
r.save('krishna.mp3')

ch.read('अथातो धर्मजिज्ञासा । चोदनालक्षणोऽर्थो धर्मः ।', ref='anuṣṭubh').save('mimamsa.mp3')
```

`chant` detects the metre and renders against the bank’s reference for it; `read` renders prose in chunks of at most 24 akṣaras. On an M3 Max a verse
renders at about five times real time.
